newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan leading brokers propose new bond repo rules.
newsitem.headline: Japan leading brokers propose new bond repo rules.

text.p: Proposed changes to trading rules governing the yen bond repo market are expected to increase market efficiency while reducing trading risks, officials at Japan's leading brokerage houses said on Monday.

The new rules, suggested by the Big Four brokerage houses at a meeting with other market participants, are aimed at standardising trade in yen bond repos and reducing market and credit risks, by allowing participants to adjust cash collateral for the borrowed bond before the settlement day.
Further talks will take place before making a final decision, but the new rules are likely to accepted by market participants, the officials said.
No target date for the implementation of the new rules has been set. Market participants would start using the new rules as soon as their computer systems are ready, brokerage house officials said.
The new rules are expected to reduce settlement-related problems which have increased with the shortening of Japanese government bond settlement period since April 21, they said.
Being closer to global standards in terms of risk management, the new rules are also expected to attract newcomers to the market, they added.
Launched in April 1996, the bond repo market is distinct from the unsecured bond borrowing/lending market in that it involves borrowing and lending bonds using cash as collateral.
Borrowers of bonds pay cash collateral to the lender at the mark-to-market price of the bonds.
On an agreed settlement day within one year or less, the borrower returns the bonds and pays borrowing fees while the counterparty repays the collateral with interest.

Under the revised rules, both parties can agree to increase of decrease collateral any time before the settlement day, as well as changing and receiving the borrowing fees and interest rates before the settlement day.
Currently such adjustments can only be made if the mark-to-market price of the bond fluctuates more than two percent.
The revised rules give the borrower of the bond the right to demand its counterparty return part of the collateral when unrealised losses are posted.
On the other hand, if an unrealised gain is reported, the lender of the bond will have the right to demand the counterparty pay extra collateral.

The balance of the bond repo market has exceeded that of the approximately 13 trillion yen Japanese government treasury bill market. It was over 20 trillion yen as of the end of May, compared with some two trillion yen when the yen bond repo trading started in April 1996, traders said. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
